preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(x) <= 200000 for line in stdin.split('\n') for x in line.split() if x.isdigit())
preconditions.description: All integers in input are within bounds 1 ≤ n ≤ m ≤ 200000 and 1 ≤ elements ≤ 200000
Input consists of exactly three lines: n m, permutation a, and permutation b

preconditions.expression: len(set(a)) == len(a) and len(set(b)) == len(b) and all(1 <= int(x) <= len(a) for x in a.split()) and all(1 <= int(x) <= len(b) for x in b.split())
preconditions.description: Permutations a and b contain distinct integers from 1 to n and 1 to m respectively, where n and m are their lengths

postconditions.description: Output is a non-negative integer representing the count of distinct integers d such that (a_i + d for all i) is a subsequence of b

postconditions.expression: all((int(a.split()[i]) + int(d) in b.split()) for i in range(len(a.split())) for d in set(int(stdout.strip())))
postconditions.description: For every d in the output set, the sequence (a_i + d for all i) must be a subsequence of b, meaning each element in the shifted a exists in b in order

postconditions.expression: all(any((int(a.split()[i]) + int(d) == int(b.split()[j])) for j in range(len(b.split()))) for i in range(len(a.split())) for d in set(int(stdout.strip())))
postconditions.description: For each d in the output set, there exists a strictly increasing sequence of indices in b where the shifted a matches b
